title: investigate and decompose goal: Close substrate gap nonzero-field-treats-an-empty-array-as-nonzero-so-returns-empty-gaps
description:
investigate and decompose goal: Close substrate gap nonzero-field-treats-an-empty-array-as-nonzero-so-returns-empty-gaps-close-false: make defect heuristic 2 in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts treat an empty array as a zero value.

Today the heuristic reads a field named by nonzero_field and returns 'absent' (defect fixed) unless the value is 0, null, undefined or "". An empty array is none of those, so a gap whose defect IS an empty result verifies as fixed while the defect is fully present. Verified live: resolving {"type":"fossilRankReport"} returns {"fossils":[],"ceiling":2000} while two source files sit over the ceiling of 2000 lines (3133 and 2780). Two fossils exist, the detector reports none, and a predicate using nonzero_field: "fossils" would close that gap as fixed.

Apply this single edit. The anchor below occurs exactly once; use it verbatim and do not re-derive or paraphrase it.

Anchor:

val === 0 || val === null

It sits on this line:

      if (val === 0 || val === null || val === undefined || val === '') {

Replace that whole line with:

      if (val === 0 || val === null || val === undefined || val === '' || (Array.isArray(val) && val.length === 0)) {

Nothing else changes. Leave the enclosing `if (nonzeroField !== null) {` block, its `return 'present';`, the following `return 'absent';`, and defect heuristics 1, 3 and 4 exactly as they are.

Rationale: nonzero_field promises "this field should be non-zero, and a zero value means the defect is still present". An empty array is the array spelling of zero — a detector that returned no findings found nothing, which is precisely the defect state. Every existing scalar case keeps its verdict; any non-empty array or non-zero scalar still returns 'absent' as before, so nothing that passes today changes.

The file must typecheck. This vessel carries a standing baseline of pre-existing test failures unrelated to this change — judge on newly-failing tests, not absolute counts.
